newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, China leaders start talks, mull future.
newsitem.headline: Russia, China leaders start talks, mull future.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Wednesday his talks with visiting Chinese President Jiang Zemin, focused on building the post-Cold War international order, could influence the future of the world.

"This meeting is of paramount importance, maybe of a historic importance because we are deciding the destiny of the 21st century," Itar-Tass news agency quoted Yeltsin as telling Jiang at the start of talks in the Kremlin.
Yeltsin and Jiang, who started a five-day state visit to Russia on Tuesday, are due to sign a political declaration later on Wednesday.

The text of the document has not been published but Yeltsin's spokesman has said it included a clause in which Beijing and Moscow would express their opposition to "claims by any country to the role of absolute leader.

Russian and Chinese officials have said that this clause is not directed at any specific country. But both states have problems with the West and appear jealous about the United States' emergence as the sole superpower in the post-Cold War world.
Yeltsin, Jiang and the leaders of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan are also due to sign a pact on Thursday reducing troops along the former Soviet-Chinese border.
